fixed_finite_expectations.static_source_reason: Three SplitN parts plus digit-only check permit 1.2.3, reject prefix-v through containsOnly, and reject 1.2 at len(parts)!=3. Each fixed component is within uint64 width. This is source reading, not observed Got.

With CoerceNewVersion=true, coerceNewVersion uses anchored loose regex with optional v and optional patch; groups become small uint64 parts and omitted patch becomes zero. String formats numeric major.minor.patch without original prefix. DetailedNewVersionErrors is true but reached only in the noncoercing branch.

Match selects slash, validation=true and caseInsensitive=false. Plain star backtracking cannot cross slash. A segment-start double star followed by slash supports zero directories and directory backtracking. Double star followed by . rather than slash falls through to ordinary star handling. ASCII literal prefix/suffix compare directly and success consumes the whole name.

There are two functions that can parse semantic versions. The `StrictNewVersion`
function only parses valid version 2 semantic versions as outlined in the
specification. The `NewVersion` function attempts to coerce a version into a
semantic version and parse it. For example, if there is a leading v or a version
listed without all 3 parts (e.g. 1.2) it will attempt to coerce it into a valid
semantic version (e.g., 1.2.0). In both cases a `Version` object is returned
that can be sorted, compared, and used in constraints.
